style.summary:
style of A: A gives repeated 'Mm-hmm' acknowledgements and no extended speech.
style of B: B speaks in a casual, filler-heavy way with 'uh' and 'you know', describing a shared resource and a generous offer.

A: A's steady 'Mm-hmm' keeps B talking and lets A shape the flow.
A's quiet style gives A the position of the one being offered the resource.
A's acknowledgements show A is the audience B is addressing.
B: B's detailed description of the server farm gives B the authority of the one who knows the resource.
B's offer to share the resource places B in the role of giver.
B's account of the earlier history 'he just got his payback' gives B the last word on the story.

A: Acknowledgements keep B talking but do not decide the flow, since B chooses what to say.
Being offered a resource puts A in a receiving role, which means B controls the offer.
Being the audience does not give A control, and B's long turns show B holds the floor.
B: B's detail is a description that A accepts, so B's authority depends on A's listening.
B's offer is conditional on scheduling, which A can accept or decline, so B does not control the outcome.
B's remark about payback is a story B tells, but A's silence means the story is B's rather than an exchange of views.

content.summary:
content of A: A offers only acknowledgements, so the substance is supplied by B.
content of B: B describes a server farm of multiprocessor machines, a colleague's use of them, and an offer to share processing time.

A: A's acknowledgements allow the content to remain on the topic A is listening to.
A's agreement shapes what is accepted as the substance.
A's silence on the content means A accepts B's account.
B: B supplies the substance of the exchange through the description of the machines.
B's offer of processing power is the main content.
B's account of the colleague's earlier use shapes the story.

A: Accepting B's account is not a choice of content, since A simply lets B's substance stand.
Agreement shapes nothing when it only confirms what B said.
Silence on the content does not show A controls it, because B alone chooses what to describe.
B: B's description is only the content A is listening to, so B's substance depends on A's attention.
B's offer is a proposal that depends on A's future needs, so its effect is not controlled by B.
B's story is a one-sided account, which shows content is shaped by whoever is willing to speak.

coordination.summary:
coordination of A: A gives backchannels and never takes an extended turn.
coordination of B: B holds the floor for almost the whole exchange and trails off at the end.

A: A's backchannels keep B speaking, which lets A manage the exchange.
A's silence keeps the turn in B's hands and so shows A decides when B stops.
A's acknowledgements do not interrupt, which keeps the flow smooth.
B: B holds the floor for the entire turn, which shows control.
B's trailing 'uh' leaves the turn open, which keeps B in charge.
B controls the length of the exchange.

A: Backchannels do not decide when B stops, since B can keep the floor as long as B wants.
Silence does not show A decides when B stops, because B chooses to trail off.
Avoiding interruption is passive and does not show A manages the flow.
B: B holds the floor because A's backchannels invite it, so the length is granted by A.
A trailing 'uh' is an unfinished thought that A could complete or let stand, so the open turn is shared.
B's length is set by A's silence, which shows A allowed B to keep going.

engagement.summary:
engagement of A: A shows engagement through steady acknowledgements.
engagement of B: B shows engagement by sharing a story and an offer of resources.

A: A's repeated 'Mm-hmm' shows A is following B closely.
A's continuous acknowledgement shows attention.
A's responsiveness keeps B talking.
B: B's story shows B is invested in the subject.
B's offer of help shows B wants the group to benefit.
B's detailed description shows B cares about the topic.

A: Repeated acknowledgement is passive and shows less investment than B's sustained speech.
Continuous attention is a sign of listening, and listening is not the same as deeper involvement.
Responsiveness keeps B talking but does not show A is more engaged than B.
B: A story shared as a passing remark shows investment, but B's trailing close suggests the point is not fully developed.
An offer of help depends on scheduling and is not something B has to follow through on, so its strength is limited.
A detailed description shows knowledge, but it is one-sided and A's input is minimal, so the engagement is not shared.
